also.hook: Altman turned artificial intelligence from a research field into a consumer phenomenon and a geopolitical agenda item. ChatGPT's November 2022 launch under his leadership put generative AI in hundreds of millions of hands, and his Senate testimony six months later, a CEO asking to be regulated, set the tone for the global governance debate this library documents.

also.moniker: The Face of the AI Boom

name: Investors
blurb: The venture and growth capital funding AI.

reading.body:
The two individuals in this dataset represent opposite poles of AI capital influence: one who shaped how billions of people encountered generative AI, and one who is quietly deploying AI inside the largest sovereign wealth fund in existence.

Sam Altman's entry is framed around reach and governance. The November 2022 ChatGPT launch moved generative AI from research infrastructure into consumer products at a scale that reoriented corporate and government priorities alike. His Senate testimony is characterized here not as a defensive act but as agenda-setting, a posture that placed one company's leadership at the center of how regulators worldwide began to think about the technology.

Stian Kirkeberg's entry is framed around institutional depth rather than public reach. A decade of cloud infrastructure work at Norway's sovereign wealth fund preceded his AI role, and the 71-member AI Ambassador network he built across four cities reflects a measured, operational approach. The data notes efficiency gains rather than speculative claims, which distinguishes this from promotional framing. What this dataset does not cover is capital amounts, portfolio composition, fund mandates, or how either figure relates to the compute, power, or physical infrastructure that constrains AI scaling. The category label is "investors," but neither entry describes investment activity in any specific sense. Readers looking for funding flows or deployment economics will not find them here.

profiles.hook: Andreessen co-created the Mosaic browser and co-founded Netscape in 1994 before co-founding the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz in 2009 with Ben Horowitz. The firm has since backed a wide range of AI companies, and Andreessen sits on the board of Meta Platforms.

profiles.hook: Son founded SoftBank in 1981 and built it into a global technology holding company. Through SoftBank's 2016 acquisition of Arm, where he now serves as chairman, and his role as chairman of the Stargate data center program announced in 2025, Son has become one of the largest capital allocators in AI infrastructure.

profiles.hook: Thiel co-founded PayPal in 1998 and, after its 2002 sale to eBay, co-founded the data analytics company Palantir Technologies in 2003 and the venture firm Founders Fund in 2005. He serves as chairman of Palantir and as a partner at Founders Fund.

profiles.hook: Hoffman co-founded LinkedIn in 2002 and later became a partner at Greylock in 2009. He was a financial backer named in OpenAI's founding announcement in December 2015, later joined OpenAI's board in 2018, and left that board in March 2023. In 2022 he co-founded Inflection AI with Mustafa Suleyman and Karen Simonyan.
profiles.name: Reid Hoffman
profiles.moniker: Co-founder, LinkedIn and Inflection AI, Partner at Greylock

profiles.hook: Khosla co-founded Sun Microsystems in 1982 and served as its founding CEO before founding Khosla Ventures in 2004. In January 2019, Khosla Ventures led a 50 million dollar investment in OpenAI, becoming the first venture firm to invest in the company.
